relevant_stock_instructions.operation: load callback and client_data from registry slot while panel registry mutex is held
indirectly invoke the previously loaded callback
lock registry, zero callback/client fields, unlock registry; no wait for copied callback

stock_panel_notifier.inference: A concurrent trigger can copy the callback and client_data, release the registry mutex, and be descheduled before the indirect call. Unregister can then clear the registry and return; the copied function pointer can still enter or continue after driver teardown.

candidate_lifecycle_observations: gf_remove sets removing before teardown; the callback exits if it observes removing or closed state.
The worker now is canceled/drained before cookie unregister, preventing late registration after unregister.
The IRQ is released in gf_remove before fp_wakelock removal; module exit unregisters the platform driver before netlink_exit.
A callback that passed the removing/opened checks before remove is not tracked or drained by the driver.
fingerprint_driver_interleaving.host_test_limit: The host panel notifier stub only counts register/unregister calls; it never dispatches a callback or models concurrent trigger/unregister. Existing host PASS therefore does not cover this boundary race.
minimal_schedule: T1: panel_event_notification_trigger locks the registry, copies callback/client_data, unlocks, then is paused before blr.
T2: gf_remove sets removing, drains screen_state_work, calls unregister; unregister clears the registry and returns without waiting for T1.
T2: remove tears down IRQ/resources and returns; module exit may continue into netlink/module teardown.
T1: resumes and invokes the copied callback, which may already have passed the removing/opened test before teardown.

canonical_docker_provider.provider_behavior: The Docker compatibility provider invokes callbacks while holding panel_client_mutex; unregister removes the list entry under the same mutex. This serializes teardown for this provider but differs from the stock full_vendor_boot module assembly.
canonical_docker_provider.interpretation: A module build against the Docker source proves compilation and ABI linkage, not the callback lifetime behavior of the stock full_vendor_boot provider.

device_observation.result: No device was listed; the active handset provider and runtime race are unverified.

resolution.reason: A driver-side in-flight counter begins only after callback entry; it cannot cover the provider interval after copying the pointer but before invoking it. The observed stock API has no unregister drain guarantee.
resolution.required_boundary: panel_event_notifier provider/API must prevent new selections and wait for all already selected callbacks before unregister returns (for example SRCU or a carefully audited per-client reference/completion scheme). Preserve the shipped callback ABI and review callback reentrancy before choosing locking.

next_gates: Identify the provider actually active on the NX809J with ADB/runtime module inventory.
Resolve unregister quiescence at the provider/API boundary for the stock implementation.
Add a deterministic concurrent trigger/unregister test against that implementation.
Rebuild the target kernel/provider and dependent module in the canonical Docker environment, then separately perform controlled phone validation.
